title: Equality before law
text: The State may not deny any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. Courts have read this article as also prohibiting arbitrary State action. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Protection of life and personal liberty
text: No person may be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Courts have interpreted this article broadly, for example in relation to the right to a fair procedure and to live with dignity. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Freedom of speech and expression
text: All citizens have the right to freedom of speech and expression. The State may impose reasonable restrictions on this freedom on grounds listed in Article 19(2), such as public order, decency or defamation. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Definition of consumer
text: A consumer is a person who buys goods or hires or avails services for a consideration. A person who obtains goods for resale or for a commercial purpose is generally not a consumer, with some exceptions for self-employment livelihood. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Definition of deficiency
text: Deficiency means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of performance of a service that is required to be maintained by law or undertaken by the person under a contract. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Manner of making a consumer complaint
text: A consumer can file a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission about defective goods, deficient services, unfair trade practices or overcharging. The complaint may be filed by the consumer, certain associations, or others as listed, and may be filed electronically. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Limitation period for consumer complaints
text: A complaint should ordinarily be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose. The Commission may admit a later complaint if the complainant shows sufficient cause for the delay. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Findings of the District Commission
text: If the District Commission is satisfied that the goods are defective or the services are deficient, it may order the opposite party to remove the defect, replace the goods, refund the price paid, pay compensation, or discontinue the unfair practice, among other directions. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Agreements that are contracts
text: An agreement is a contract if it is made with the free consent of parties who are competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and is not expressly declared void. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Compensation for breach of contract
text: A party who suffers from a breach of contract is entitled to receive compensation for loss or damage that naturally arose in the usual course of things from the breach, or that the parties knew when contracting was likely to result. Remote or indirect loss is not compensated. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Compensation where a penalty is stipulated
text: When a contract names a sum payable on breach, or a penalty, the party complaining of breach is entitled to reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named, whether or not actual damage is proved. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Punishment for identity theft
text: Fraudulently or dishonestly using another person's electronic signature, password or other unique identification feature is punishable with imprisonment of up to three years and a fine. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Cheating by personation using a computer resource
text: Cheating by personation by means of a communication device or computer resource is punishable with imprisonment of up to three years and a fine. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Compensation for unauthorised access to computer systems
text: A person who accesses, copies, damages or disrupts a computer, computer system or network without the permission of its owner is liable to pay compensation to the person affected. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Definition of lease
text: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of the right to enjoy the property for a certain time, express or implied, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Duration of certain leases and notice to terminate
text: Where there is no written contract or local law fixing the lease term, a lease for agricultural or manufacturing purposes is treated as year to year and a lease for other purposes as month to month. Termination needs written notice of the period the section prescribes (six months or fifteen days respectively). (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Documents that must be registered
text: Certain documents must be registered, including leases of immovable property from year to year or for a term exceeding one year. An unregistered document that requires registration has limited effect as evidence. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Grounds for divorce
text: Either spouse may petition for divorce on specified grounds, which include cruelty and desertion for a continuous period of at least two years, among other grounds listed in the section. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Application to the Magistrate for relief
act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
text: An aggrieved person, a Protection Officer or anyone on her behalf may apply to the Magistrate for one or more reliefs under the Act, such as protection orders, residence orders and monetary relief. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Conditions before retrenchment of a workman
text: A workman with a year of continuous service may be retrenched only after one month's written notice or wages in lieu, payment of retrenchment compensation (fifteen days' average pay for each completed year of service) and notice to the appropriate Government. NOTE: labour law has been reorganised into new Labour Codes; check whether this Act still applies. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Payment of gratuity
text: Gratuity is payable to an employee on superannuation, retirement, resignation, or death or disablement, generally after five years of continuous service, at the rate of fifteen days' wages for each completed year of service. NOTE: check whether the Code on Social Security, 2020 now governs gratuity. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Cheating
text: Whoever deceives a person and fraudulently or dishonestly induces them to deliver property, or intentionally induces them to do or omit something they would not otherwise do, commits cheating. The Sanhita replaced the Indian Penal Code from 1 July 2024. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)

title: Theft
text: Whoever intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to take it, commits theft. The Sanhita replaced the Indian Penal Code from 1 July 2024. (Paraphrased summary by the project author; compare with the official text before relying on it.)
